title_en: Chinese History (17/20): The Gaokao, the Exam That Changes Lives
note_en: 几乎 means "almost," and it often comes right before 能 to say something is just barely possible: 几乎能听到笔尖划过纸面的声音 "you can almost hear the pens scratching across the paper." Like English "almost," it goes before the verb, but notice that Chinese needs no "you" here; the sentence simply has no subject. 几乎 also softens a strong verb: 高考成绩几乎决定了… "gaokao scores all but decide..."
